question.problem:
Consider the function $y=(\operatorname{sec}⁡x)^{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}.$ Its derivative is given by

$$
{y}^{′}=(\operatorname{sec}⁡x)^{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}\cdot g(x).
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=(\operatorname{sec}⁡x)^{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((\operatorname{sec}⁡x)^{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{tan}⁡x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)^{′}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡x))+(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡x))}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & ={sec}^{2}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡x)+\operatorname{tan}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\operatorname{sec}⁡x) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & ={sec}^{2}⁡x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡x)+{tan}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y({sec}^{2}⁡x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡x)+{tan}^{2}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=(\operatorname{sec}⁡x)^{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =(\operatorname{sec}⁡x)^{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}({sec}^{2}⁡x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡x)+{tan}^{2}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)={sec}^{2}⁡x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡x)+{tan}^{2}⁡x.$
